context_requirements: Expression of CYP11A1, CYP11B1, or ESR1 (or related steroidogenic/nuclear receptor pathway components)
Intact apoptotic machinery (caspases, BAX/BAK) for late apoptotic transcriptional program
Proliferating cells for antiproliferative/cytostatic transcriptional signature
TP53 wild-type or functional for robust CDKN1A/GADD45 induction (many lines are mutant)
falsifiers: No significant change in any of the listed proximal or late genes at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine cell lines
Predominant upregulation of proliferation genes (e.g., CCND1, MYC, MKI67) rather than downregulation
Absence of apoptosis-related gene changes at 24 h despite strong antiproliferative effects
Line responses completely uncorrelated with ESR1, CYP11A1, or CYP11B1 expression

evidence.supports: Vitamin E succinate is a potent antineoplastic agent that induces apoptosis and inhibits proliferation, with p53-independent effects.
6-mercaptopurine, an antineoplastic agent, activates the orphan nuclear receptor Nurr1, showing that antineoplastics can directly regulate transcription factors.
Ixabepilone, an antineoplastic agent, stabilizes microtubules leading to arrested tumor cell division and apoptosis.
beta-Elemene, a plant-derived antineoplastic agent, triggers apoptosis in lung cancer cells via Bax upregulation and Bcl-2 downregulation.
Etoposide, an antineoplastic agent, inhibits cell cycle progression at late S/G2 and causes DNA damage, leading to cell cycle arrest and apoptosis.
